industry.why: Neutral at industry level, carried, with the sector rows carrying the view. Component 1 regime, 23-Oct-26 (risk-off confirmed and broadening: the discount-rate squeeze now a positioning wash-out in the artificial intelligence complex with credit leading it, bonds rallied as a hedge for the first time this cycle while the Fed still hikes in December, the US 10-year near 5.10%, Brent $111, French sovereign stress spilling into Italy, European defensives leading cyclicals on all five windows and breadth in the bottom fifth of three years; sources present 2026-W43): technology saw $5.5 billion of net selling in the week, the most since January 2025 (Jefferies, 17 Oct), the rotation came out of it, and Wood says 'the easy money in semis is made'; against that, Jefferies finds sector pockets still upgrading inside it (analogue chips, optical networking, artificial-intelligence memory) and Morgan Stanley still rates North American semiconductors Attractive. Relative strength per 31-relative-strength.md, 2026-10-23 against 2026-08-21, not week on week: B now, B prior at industry level, carried by Semiconductors at A. The industry row stays C because the industry is split: Semiconductors (D), Software B2B Enterprise (D), Fintech (D) and Games (D) carry the Underweight; IT services, Hardware and vertical software stay Neutral. Counter-case for D: the heaviest net selling in 21 months is a regime statement; for B: the only industry with upgrades inside the sell-off.

sector.why: Neutral, from Underweight. Component 1 regime, 9-Oct-26 (late-cycle rates squeeze turning into a European credit-and-sovereign stress episode: hiking path re-marked up, credit joined rates, French spread 152 basis points, European breadth at three-year lows on all four averages, index 5.3% off its high, defensives turning over one and four weeks but unconfirmed, growth firm at the level; sources present 2026-W41): the Underweight was set on 'discretionary corporate spend cut first in a slowdown' with sources absent, and the growth data this week show no slowdown (United States GDP tracking 3.1%, euro area PMIs 52.9 and 53.0, Goldman Sachs 5 to 8 Oct); balanced. Relative strength per 31-relative-strength.md, 2026-10-09 against 2026-08-07, not week on week: B now, C prior; the turning note's first hypothesis names the consultancies (Capgemini, Sopra) turning on sovereign programmes, with Alten, Indra and Kainos in the MI Pool, weighed as a brainstorm. Counter-case: no source spoke to IT services or software, the artificial-intelligence-replacement fear that de-rated the group is being tested, not disproved, and corporate budgets are the first cut if the margin rolls over; back to D if sell-side momentum on the three MI Pool names (today C, B, D) falls.

geography.why: Double Underweight, carried unchanged on this week's reading. Goldman Sachs (16 Oct) has French spreads at decade highs with tentative spillover to Italy and judges France's fiscal challenge 'harder now than in 2011-15'; the premium in basis points was not read, so the reversal conditions (back to D under 120 basis points, to C under 100) could not be tested and are plainly not met at a decade high. Component 1 regime, 23-Oct-26 (risk-off confirmed and broadening: the discount-rate squeeze now a positioning wash-out in the artificial intelligence complex with credit leading it, bonds rallied as a hedge for the first time this cycle while the Fed still hikes in December, the US 10-year near 5.10%, Brent $111, French sovereign stress spilling into Italy, European defensives leading cyclicals on all five windows and breadth in the bottom fifth of three years; sources present 2026-W43). Relative strength is not graded by country; no live holding is French-listed. Counter-case unchanged: a country letter is a blunt tool on 110 stocks and lands on French-listed global businesses (TotalEnergies, whose memo exposures lift its Thematic Fit/Momentum by two grades through the stock layer; Soitec; Sopra Steria; Alten) as hard as on domestic banks and property; and Goldman's own judgement is that disorderly escalation is less likely than in 2011-15.
